```{r, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

df_analysis <- read_csv(here("data/analysis.csv"))
head(df_analysis)
dim(df_analysis) # 14575x484
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
df_clean <- df_analysis[, -(6:58)] 
df_clean <- df_clean |> select(- "dateTimeSample", - "dateProcessed")
head(df_clean)
# there are 326 frequencies
```
# Introduction

# Dealing with missing values
```{r, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

# Count missing values for each frequency, by species
missing_df <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    across(starts_with("F"), ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("F"),
    names_to = "frequency",
    values_to = "missing_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(frequency = as.numeric(sub("^F", "", frequency)))

# Plot
ggplot(missing_df, aes(x = frequency, y = missing_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Missing Frequency Measurements by Species",
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Number of Missing Values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Notice the pattern in Figure 1, there are two ranges of frequencies with missing values: F90-F170 and F173-F260. Frequencies F90-F170 are missing for all three species, for almost 3000 observations for LT, 800 for LW and 300 for SMB. Lastly, there are 183 observations in LT with missing values. As shown in Figure 2, there is at least one missing value in 9 LT, 3 LW and 2 SMB. The fish LT008 is the only one missing values between F173-F260, hence we remove it from the dataset.

```{r, include=FALSE}
df_clean <- df_clean |>
  filter(fishNum != "LT008")
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Count missing frequency values for each fish
missing_fish <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(species, fishNum) %>%
  summarise(
    missing_count = sum(is.na(pick(starts_with("F")))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot
ggplot(missing_fish, aes(x = fishNum, y = missing_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Missing Frequency Measurements by Individual Fish",
    x = "Fish ID",
    y = "Number of Missing Values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
missing_fish <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(species, fishNum) %>%
  summarise(
    missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(as.matrix(pick(starts_with("F"))))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(missing_fish, aes(x = fishNum, y = missing_pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Missing Measurements by Fish",
    x = "Fish ID",
    y = "Missing Measurements (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Some fish may be missing more values simply because they have more fish as shown by Figure 2, so we observe Figure 3 which shows percentage of values missing for each fish to account for this. Among fish with missing observations, approximately 35% of frequency measurements are consistently missing, primarily within the F90–F170 range. This suggests a systematic pattern of missingness rather than isolated missing values. While some imputation methods were considered to replace missing values, given the small number of fish in the sample, the consequences of imputing missing values are unknown, and specially when focusing on dimensionality reduction we want to avoid introducing more noise than there already is to perceive signals clearly. Consequently, we drop any rows that have missing values in the frequencies (4,242 in total).

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Remove rows with missing frequency measurements
freq_cols <- grep("^F[0-9]", names(df_clean), value = TRUE)

df_complete <- df_clean[
  complete.cases(df_clean[, freq_cols]),
]
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)

table4 <- df_complete %>%
  group_by(species, fishNum) %>%
  summarise(pings = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    `Number of fish` = n(),
    `Total pings` = sum(pings),
    `Median pings` = median(pings),
    `Min. pings` = min(pings),
    `Max. pings` = max(pings),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(
  table4,
  caption = "Overview of the dataset with no missing values",
  digits = 1,
  format = "pipe"
)

```

## Exploration
```{r, include=FALSE}
library(corrplot)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Select frequency measurements only
X <- df_complete[, grepl("^F[0-9]", names(df_complete))]

# Calculate empirical correlation matrix
R_empirical <- cor(X)

# Plot correlation matrix
corrplot(
  R_empirical,
  method = "color",
  type = "lower",
  tl.pos = "n",
  diag = FALSE,
  title = "Fish frequency correlation matrix (All pings)",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
  font.main = 1
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Since each fish contributes multiple pings, correlations in Figure 4 describe relationships across all pings, not across independent fish. Next, we average all frequencies by fish, to obtain one row per fish and plot the correlation matrix again.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
df_avg <- df_complete %>%
  group_by(fishNum, species) %>%
  summarise(
    across(starts_with("F"), mean),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Extract frequency measurements
X_avg <- df_avg %>%
  select(starts_with("F")) %>%
  select(-"fishNum")

# Calculate correlations
R_avg <- cor(X_avg)

# Plot
corrplot(
  R_avg,
  method = "color",
  type = "lower",
  tl.pos = "n",
  diag = FALSE,
  title = "Correlation Matrix (One Average Measurement per Fish)",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
  font.main = 1
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(123)  # Reproducibility

df_random <- df_complete %>%
  group_by(fishNum, species) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Correlation matrix
# Select only frequency columns
X_random <- df_random[, grepl("^F[0-9]", names(df_random))]

# Calculate correlations
R_random <- cor(X_random)

# Plot
corrplot(
  R_random,
  method = "color",
  type = "lower",
  tl.pos = "n",
  diag = FALSE,
  title = "Correlation Matrix (One Random Ping per Fish)",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
  font.main = 1
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Set up 2x2 plot
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

for (i in 1:4) {

  # Different random sample each time
  set.seed(123 + i)

  df_random <- df_complete %>%
    group_by(fishNum, species) %>%
    slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
    ungroup()

  # Select frequency columns
  X_random <- df_random[, grepl("^F[0-9]", names(df_random))]

  # Calculate correlation matrix
  R_random <- cor(X_random)

  # Plot
  corrplot(
    R_random,
    method = "color",
    type = "lower",
    tl.pos = "n",
    diag = FALSE,
    title = paste("Random Sample", i),
    mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
    font.main = 1
  )
}

# Reset plotting layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Closer frequencies are highly correlated

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Extract frequency values
freq <- as.numeric(sub("F", "", colnames(R_avg)))

# Get all unique frequency pairs
pairs <- which(upper.tri(R_avg), arr.ind = TRUE)

# Calculate distance and correlation for each pair
distance <- abs(freq[pairs[, 1]] - freq[pairs[, 2]])
correlation <- R_avg[pairs]

# Plot
plot(
  distance, correlation,
  pch = 16, cex = 0.2,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15),
  xlab = "Distance between frequencies",
  ylab = "Pearson correlation",
  main = "Correlation vs. Frequency Distance (Average per fish)"
)

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Extract frequency values
freq <- as.numeric(sub("F", "", colnames(R_empirical)))

# Get all unique frequency pairs
pairs <- which(upper.tri(R_empirical), arr.ind = TRUE)

# Calculate frequency distance and correlation
distance <- abs(freq[pairs[, 1]] - freq[pairs[, 2]])
correlation <- R_empirical[pairs]

# Plot
plot(
  distance, correlation,
  pch = 16, cex = 0.2,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15),
  xlab = "Distance between frequencies",
  ylab = "Pearson correlation",
  main = "Correlation vs. Frequency Distance (All Pings)"
)

```
